{{Short description|Abstract mathematical group}}
In [[abstract algebra]], the '''Virasoro group''' or '''Bott–Virasoro group''' (often denoted by ''Vir''){{sfnp|Bahns|Bauer|Witt|2016}} is an [[Lie group#Infinite-dimensional Lie groups|infinite-dimensional Lie group]] defined as the universal [[Group extension#Central extension|central extension]] of the [[Diffeomorphism#Diffeomorphism group|group of diffeomorphisms]] of the [[circle]]. The corresponding [[Lie algebra]] is the [[Virasoro algebra]], which has a key role in [[conformal field theory]] (CFT) and [[string theory]].

The group is named after [[Miguel Ángel Virasoro (physicist)|Miguel Ángel Virasoro]] and [[Raoul Bott]].

==Background==
An [[Orientability|orientation-preserving]] [[diffeomorphism]] of the circle <math>S^1</math>, whose points are labelled by a real coordinate <math>x</math> subject to the identification <math>x\sim x+2\pi</math>, is a [[Smoothness|smooth]] map <math>f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}:x\mapsto f(x)</math> such that <math>f(x+2\pi)=f(x)+2\pi</math> and <math>f'(x)>0</math>. The set of all such maps spans a group, with [[binary operation|multiplication]] given by the [[Function composition|composition]] of diffeomorphisms. This group is the [[universal cover]] of the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the circle, denoted as <math>\widetilde{\text{Diff}}{}^+(S^1)</math>.

==Definition==
The Virasoro group is the universal central extension of <math>\widetilde{\text{Diff}}{}^+(S^1)</math>.{{sfnp|Guieu|Roger|2007|loc=section 4.4}} The extension is defined by a specific [[Group cohomology#Definitions|two-cocycle]], which is a real-valued function <math>\mathsf{C}(f,g)</math> of pairs of diffeomorphisms. Specifically, the extension is defined by the Bott–Thurston cocycle:
<math display="block">
\mathsf{C}(f,g)
\equiv
-\frac{1}{48\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
\log\big[(f\circ g)'(x)\big]
\frac{g''(x)\,\text{d}x}{g'(x)}.
</math>
In these terms, the Virasoro group is the set <math>\widetilde{\text{Diff}}{}^+(S^1)\times\mathbb{R}</math> of all pairs <math>(f,\alpha)</math>, where <math>f</math> is a diffeomorphism and <math>\alpha</math> is a [[real number]], endowed with the binary operation
<math display="block">
(f,\alpha)\cdot(g,\beta)
=
\big(f\circ g,\alpha+\beta+\mathsf{C}(f,g)\big).
</math>
This operation is an associative group operation. This extension is the only central extension of the universal cover of the group of circle diffeomorphisms, up to trivial extensions.{{sfnp|Guieu|Roger|2007}} The Virasoro group can also be defined without the use explicit coordinates or an explicit choice of [[Group cohomology|cocycle]] to represent the central extension, via a description the [[Covering space#Universal covering|universal cover]] of the group.{{sfnp|Guieu|Roger|2007}}

== Virasoro algebra ==
{{Main|Virasoro algebra}}

The [[Lie algebra]] of the Virasoro group is the [[Virasoro algebra]]. As a [[vector space]], the Lie algebra of the Virasoro group consists of pairs <math>(\xi,\alpha)</math>, where <math>\xi=\xi(x)\partial_x</math> is a [[vector field]] on the circle and <math>\alpha</math> is a real number as before. The vector field, in particular, can be seen as an [[infinitesimal]] diffeomorphism <math>f(x)=x+\epsilon\xi(x)</math>. The Lie bracket of pairs <math>(\xi,\alpha)</math> then follows from the multiplication defined above, and can be shown to satisfy{{sfnp|Oblak|2017|loc=section 6.4}}
:<math>\big[(\xi,\alpha),(\zeta,\beta)\big]=\bigg([\xi,\zeta],-\frac{1}{24\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\text{d}x\,\xi(x)\zeta'''(x)\bigg)</math>
where the bracket of vector fields on the right-hand side is the [[Lie bracket of vector fields|usual one]]: <math>[\xi,\zeta]=(\xi(x)\zeta'(x)-\zeta(x)\xi'(x))\partial_x</math>. Upon defining the complex generators
<math display="block">
L_m\equiv\Big(-ie^{imx}\partial_x,-\frac{i}{24}\delta_{m,0}\Big),
\qquad
Z\equiv (0,-i),
</math>
the Lie bracket takes the standard textbook form of the Virasoro algebra:{{sfnp|Di Francesco|Mathieu|Sénéchal|1997}}
<math display="block">
[L_m,L_n]
=
(m-n)L_{m+n}+\frac{Z}{12}m(m^2-1)\delta_{m+n}.
</math>

The generator <math>Z</math> [[Commutative property|commutes]] with the whole algebra. Since its presence is due to a central extension, it is subject to a [[superselection]] rule which guarantees that, in any [[physical system]] having Virasoro symmetry, the operator representing <math>Z</math> is a multiple of the identity. The coefficient in front of the identity is then known as a [[central charge]].

==Properties==
Since each diffeomorphism <math>f</math> must be specified by infinitely many parameters (for instance the [[Fourier series|Fourier modes]] of the periodic function <math>f(x)-x</math>), the Virasoro group is infinite-dimensional.

===Coadjoint representation===
The Lie bracket of the Virasoro algebra can be viewed as a differential of the [[adjoint representation]] of the Virasoro group. Its dual, the [[coadjoint representation]] of the Virasoro group, provides the transformation law of a CFT [[stress–energy tensor|stress tensor]] under conformal transformations. From this perspective, the [[Schwarzian derivative]] in this transformation law emerges as a consequence of the Bott–Thurston cocycle; in fact, the Schwarzian is the so-called Souriau cocycle (referring to [[Jean-Marie Souriau]]) associated with the Bott–Thurston cocycle.{{sfnp|Guieu|Roger|2007}}
